problem.summary: 深度卷积网络在图像识别中取得巨大进展，但如何结合Inception架构的计算效率与残差连接的训练加速效果是一个开放问题。

motivation.summary: 残差连接在传统架构中取得了与Inception-v3相似的性能，但将两者结合是否能带来益处尚不明确。同时，需要设计更高效、更统一的Inception架构变体。

core_idea.summary: 提出三种新架构：纯Inception-v4、Inception-ResNet-v1和Inception-ResNet-v2，通过实证研究残差连接对Inception网络训练速度和最终精度的影响，并引入残差缩放技术以稳定训练。

method.summary: 设计统一的Inception模块（A、B、C）和缩减模块，将残差连接引入Inception架构，并在残差分支末端使用线性激活和缩放（约0.1倍）以稳定训练。使用RMSProp优化器和指数学习率衰减进行训练。

experiments.summary: 在ILSVRC 2012分类任务上评估单模型单裁剪、多裁剪（10/12、144）以及集成性能。比较了Inception-v3、Inception-v4、Inception-ResNet-v1和Inception-ResNet-v2的训练曲线和最终错误率。

claims.claim: 残差连接显著加速Inception网络的训练。
残差Inception网络在相似计算成本下，最终精度略优于非残差版本。
Inception-v4和Inception-ResNet-v2在单模型性能上达到新的最优水平。
适当的残差缩放可以稳定非常宽的残差Inception网络的训练。
集成模型在ImageNet测试集上达到3.08%的top-5错误率。

limitations.limitation: 残差连接带来的最终精度提升幅度较小（“thin margin”）。
Inception-v4的实际步进时间比残差版本慢，可能由于层数更多。
为了在单GPU上训练，Inception-ResNet版本未在求和层后使用批归一化，这可能不是最优选择。
集成性能的提升不如单模型性能提升显著。

nodes.title: 输入茎（Stem）
nodes.label: 输入处理
nodes.summary: 网络的初始部分，将299x299x3的输入图像逐步降维并提取特征。
nodes.description: 由一系列卷积和池化层组成，将输入尺寸从299x299x3转换为35x35x384（对于Inception-v4和Inception-ResNet-v2）或35x35x256（对于Inception-ResNet-v1）。具体结构见图3和图14。

nodes.title: Inception-A模块
nodes.label: 特征提取模块
nodes.summary: 处理35x35网格尺寸的Inception模块，用于提取多尺度特征。
nodes.description: 在Inception-v4中，该模块包含多个并行的1x1和3x3卷积分支以及一个平均池化分支，最后进行滤波器拼接。具体结构见图4。在Inception-ResNet-v1/v2中，对应的残差版本（Inception-ResNet-A）结构略有不同，但核心思想类似。

nodes.title: 缩减-A模块（Reduction-A）
nodes.label: 空间降维
nodes.summary: 将特征图的空间尺寸从35x35降低到17x17。
nodes.description: 该模块使用多个并行的卷积和最大池化操作来实现降维。不同网络变体的滤波器数量（k, l, m, n）不同，具体参数见表1。结构见图7。

nodes.title: Inception-B模块
nodes.label: 特征提取模块
nodes.description: 在Inception-v4中，该模块使用1x7和7x1的非对称卷积。具体结构见图5。在Inception-ResNet-v1/v2中，对应的残差版本（Inception-ResNet-B）结构见图11和图17。

nodes.title: 缩减-B模块（Reduction-B）
nodes.label: 空间降维
nodes.summary: 将特征图的空间尺寸从17x17降低到8x8。
nodes.description: 该模块用于进一步降低空间分辨率。Inception-v4和Inception-ResNet-v1/v2使用不同的缩减-B模块。具体结构见图8、图12和图18。

nodes.title: Inception-C模块
nodes.label: 特征提取模块
nodes.description: 在Inception-v4中，该模块使用1x3和3x1的卷积。具体结构见图6。在Inception-ResNet-v1/v2中，对应的残差版本（Inception-ResNet-C）结构见图13和图19。

nodes.title: 残差连接与缩放
nodes.label: 核心创新
nodes.summary: 在Inception-ResNet中，将Inception模块的输出通过1x1卷积线性扩展后，与输入相加，并乘以一个缩放因子（约0.1）以稳定训练。
nodes.description: 每个残差Inception块后接一个1x1卷积（无激活函数）进行滤波器扩展，然后与输入相加。为了稳定训练，对残差分支的输出乘以一个常数缩放因子（通常在0.1左右）。这解决了当滤波器数量超过1000时训练不稳定的问题。

nodes.title: 分类头
nodes.label: 输出层
nodes.summary: 网络的最后部分，包括平均池化、Dropout和Softmax分类层。
nodes.description: 在8x8特征图后进行平均池化，然后应用Dropout（保留概率0.8），最后通过全连接层和Softmax输出1000类预测。

edges.label: 特征传递
edges.description: 输入茎的输出传递给Inception-A模块进行特征提取。

edges.label: 空间降维
edges.description: Inception-A模块的输出通过缩减-A模块降低空间分辨率。

edges.label: 特征传递
edges.description: 缩减-A模块的输出传递给Inception-B模块。

edges.label: 空间降维
edges.description: Inception-B模块的输出通过缩减-B模块进一步降低空间分辨率。

edges.label: 特征传递
edges.description: 缩减-B模块的输出传递给Inception-C模块。

edges.label: 特征传递
edges.description: Inception-C模块的输出传递给分类头进行最终预测。

edges.label: 残差分支输入
edges.description: 在Inception-ResNet中，Inception-A模块的输出作为残差分支的输入。

edges.label: 残差相加
edges.description: 残差分支的输出（经缩放）与原始输入相加，形成残差连接。

deltas.before: Inception模块使用滤波器拼接作为聚合方式。
deltas.after: 在Inception-ResNet中，使用残差连接（加法）替代滤波器拼接，并在残差分支末端使用线性激活和缩放。
deltas.why_it_matters: 残差连接显著加速了训练过程（见图21-24），并可能略微提升最终精度。缩放技术解决了宽残差网络训练不稳定的问题。

deltas.before: Inception网络架构设计较为复杂，不同网格尺寸的模块设计不统一。
deltas.after: Inception-v4采用了更统一、简化的架构设计，为每个网格尺寸（35x35, 17x17, 8x8）设计了标准化的Inception模块（A, B, C）。
deltas.why_it_matters: 简化了架构，使其更易于理解和实现，同时保持了高性能。

deltas.before: 训练Inception网络时，需要仔细调整各层尺寸以平衡计算。
deltas.after: 使用残差连接后，可以使用更“廉价”的Inception块，并通过1x1卷积进行滤波器扩展。
deltas.why_it_matters: 在保持或提升性能的同时，可能优化了计算效率。

formulas.description: 残差连接的基本形式，其中F是残差函数（例如一个Inception块），x是输入，y是输出。

variables.name: F(x, \{W_i\})
variables.description: 残差函数，由一组权重W_i参数化的子网络（如Inception块）

formulas.intuition: 通过恒等映射（跳跃连接）让网络更容易学习残差F(x)，而不是直接学习目标映射，这有助于训练非常深的网络。

formulas.description: 带缩放的残差连接，其中α是一个小的常数（如0.1），用于稳定训练。

variables.name: F(x, \{W_i\})
variables.description: 残差函数，通常是线性激活（无ReLU）后的Inception块输出

formulas.intuition: 当残差分支的滤波器数量很多（>1000）时，直接相加会导致训练不稳定。通过乘以一个小的缩放因子α，可以防止激活值过大，从而稳定训练过程。

formulas.description: 交叉熵损失函数，用于图像分类任务。这是训练目标，但论文中未明确给出公式。
formulas.intuition: 标准的分类损失函数，用于衡量模型预测分布与真实标签分布之间的差异。

main_result.description: 在ILSVRC 2012验证集上，单模型单裁剪评估。Inception-v4和Inception-ResNet-v2达到最低的top-1和top-5错误率。

ablation.description: 比较有无残差连接对训练速度和最终精度的影响。残差版本训练更快，但最终精度提升有限。

results.observation: 残差版本训练速度显著更快，但最终top-1错误率略高（21.3% vs 21.2%），top-5错误率略低（5.5% vs 5.6%）。
残差版本训练速度更快，最终精度略优（top-1: 19.9% vs 20.0%, top-5: 4.9% vs 5.0%）。

robustness.description: 论文未进行传统意义上的鲁棒性测试（如对抗样本、分布外泛化）。但研究了残差缩放对训练稳定性的影响。

results.observation: 当滤波器数量超过1000时，未缩放的残差网络训练不稳定（“died”）。使用缩放因子（约0.1）可以稳定训练。

scaling.description: 比较了不同模型大小（Inception-v3/ResNet-v1 vs Inception-v4/ResNet-v2）对性能的影响。更大的模型（v4/v2）性能更好。

results.observation: 最终精度主要取决于模型大小，而非是否使用残差连接。更大的Inception-v4和Inception-ResNet-v2模型优于较小的Inception-v3和Inception-ResNet-v1。

case_study.description: 论文分析了集成模型的分类错误，并指出集成模型尚未达到标注噪声的水平，仍有改进空间。

results.observation: 集成模型的错误率（3.08% top-5）仍高于数据集标注的噪声水平，表明存在系统性错误。

terms.definition: 一种卷积神经网络架构，其核心思想是在同一层内使用不同尺寸的卷积核（如1x1, 3x3, 5x5）和池化操作，并将它们的输出拼接起来，以捕获多尺度特征。
一种网络连接方式，将层的输入直接加到其输出上，即 y = F(x) + x。这有助于梯度流动，使得训练非常深的网络成为可能。
Inception架构中，将来自不同卷积/池化分支的输出张量在通道维度上拼接起来的操作。
在残差连接中，对残差分支F(x)的输出乘以一个小的常数（如0.1）的技术，用于稳定训练，特别是在网络很宽（滤波器数量多）时。
ImageNet大规模视觉识别挑战赛2012，是一个广泛使用的图像分类基准数据集，包含1000个类别。
图像分类任务的评估指标。Top-1错误率是指模型预测的最可能类别不是正确类别的比例。Top-5错误率是指正确类别不在模型预测的前五个最可能类别中的比例。

steps.description: 1. 准备ILSVRC 2012数据集，并进行标准预处理（如缩放至299x299）。
2. 根据论文中的图表（图3-19）实现Inception-v4、Inception-ResNet-v1和Inception-ResNet-v2的网络架构。特别注意残差缩放（约0.1倍）的实现。
3. 设置训练环境：使用RMSProp优化器（衰减0.9，ε=1.0），初始学习率0.045，每两个epoch乘以0.94进行指数衰减。
4. 使用分布式训练（如20个GPU副本）进行模型训练。监控训练曲线，确保残差网络训练稳定。
5. 在验证集上评估单模型性能（单裁剪、多裁剪）。使用论文中描述的裁剪策略（如12裁剪、144裁剪）。
6. 训练多个模型副本（如4个）并进行集成，评估集成性能。

metadata.title: Inception-v4, Inception-ResNet and the Impact of Residual Connections on Learning
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / CNN / Top-cited ML method paper
metadata.abstract: Very deep convolutional networks have been central to the largest advances in image recognition performance in recent years. One example is the Inception architecture that has been shown to achieve very good performance at relatively low computational cost. Recently, the introduction of residual connections in conjunction with a more traditional architecture has yielded state-of-the-art performance in the 2015 ILSVRC challenge; its performance was similar to the latest generation Inception-v3 network. This raises the question: Are there any benefits to combining Inception architectures with residual connections? Here we give clear empirical evidence that training with residual connections accelerates the training of Inception networks significantly. There is also some evidence of residual Inception networks outperforming similarly expensive Inception networks without residual connections by a thin margin. We also present several new streamlined architectures for both residual and non-residual Inception networks. These variations improve the single-frame recognition performance on the ILSVRC 2012 classification task significantly. We further demonstrate how proper activation scaling stabilizes the training of very wide residual Inception networks. With an ensemble of three residual and one Inception-v4 networks, we achieve 3.08% top-5 error on the test set of the ImageNet classification (CLS) challenge.

Abstract
Very deep convolutional networks have been central to
the largest advances in image recognition performance in

recent years. One example is the Inception architecture that has been shown to achieve very good performance at rel- atively low computational cost. Recently, the introduction of residual connections in conjunction with a more tradi- tional architecture has yielded state-of-the-art performance in the 2015 ILSVRC challenge; its performance was similar to the latest generation Inception-v3 network. This raises the question of whether there are any beneﬁt in combining the Inception architecture with residual connections. Here we give clear empirical evidence that training with residual connections accelerates the training of Inception networks signiﬁcantly. There is also some evidence of residual Incep-
tion networks outperforming similarly expensive Inception
networks without residual connections by a thin margin. We

also present several new streamlined architectures for both residual and non-residual Inception networks. These varia- tions improve the single-frame recognition performance on the ILSVRC 2012 classiﬁcation task signiﬁcantly. We fur- ther demonstrate how proper activation scaling stabilizes the training of very wide residual Inception networks. With an ensemble of three residual and one Inception-v4, we achieve 3.08% top-5 error on the test set of the ImageNet classiﬁcation (CLS) challenge. 1. Introduction Since the 2012 ImageNet competition [11] winning en- try by Krizhevsky et al [8], their network “AlexNet” has
been successfully applied to a larger variety of computer

vision tasks, for example to object-detection [4], segmen- tation [10], human pose estimation [17], video classiﬁca- tion [7], object tracking [18], and superresolution [3]. These examples are but a few of all the applications to which deep convolutional networks have been very successfully applied ever since. In this work we study the combination of the two most recent ideas: Residual connections introduced by He et al. in [5] and the latest revised version of the Inception archi-
tecture [15]. In [5], it is argued that residual connections are

of inherent importance for training very deep architectures. Since Inception networks tend to be very deep, it is natu- ral to replace the ﬁlter concatenation stage of the Inception architecture with residual connections. This would allow Inception to reap all the beneﬁts of the residual approach while retaining its computational efﬁciency. Besides a straightforward integration, we have also stud- ied whether Inception itself can be made more efﬁcient by making it deeper and wider. For that purpose, we designed a new version named Inception-v4 which has a more uni- form simpliﬁed architecture and more inception modules than Inception-v3. Historically, Inception-v3 had inherited a lot of the baggage of the earlier incarnations. The techni- cal constraints chieﬂy came from the need for partitioning the model for distributed training using DistBelief [2]. Now, after migrating our training setup to TensorFlow [1] these constraints have been lifted, which allowed us to simplify the archite...
lenge [11] dataset. The last experiment reported here is an evaluation of an
ensemble of all the best performing models presented here.

As it was apparent that both Inception-v4 and Inception- ResNet-v2 performed similarly well, exceeding state-of- the art single frame performance on the ImageNet valida- tion dataset, we wanted to see how a combination of those pushes the state of the art on this well studied dataset. Sur- prisingly, we found that gains on the single-frame perfor-
mance do not translate into similarly large gains on ensem-

bled performance. Nonetheless, it still allows us to report 3.1% top-5 error on the validation set with four models en- sembled setting a new state of the art, to our best knowl- edge. In the last section, we study some of the classiﬁcation failures and conclude that the ensemble still has not reached the label noise of the annotations on this dataset and there is still room for improvement for the predictions. 2. Related Work
Convolutional networks have become popular in large

scale image recognition tasks after Krizhevsky et al. [8]. Some of the next important milestones were Network-in- network [9] by Lin et al., VGGNet [12] by Simonyan et al. and GoogLeNet (Inception-v1) [14] by Szegedy et al. Residual connection were introduced by He et al. in [5] in which they give convincing theoretical and practical ev- idence for the advantages of utilizing additive merging of signals both for image recognition, and especially for object
detection. The authors argue that residual connections are

inherently necessary for training very deep convolutional models. Our ﬁndings do not seem to support this view, at least for image recognition. However it might require more measurement points with deeper architectures to understand the true extent of beneﬁcial aspects offered by residual con- nections. In the experimental section we demonstrate that it is not very difﬁcult to train competitive very deep net- works without utilizing residual connections. However the use of residual connections seems to improve the training
speed greatly, which is alone a great argument for their use.

The Inception deep convolutional architecture was intro- duced in [14] and was called GoogLeNet or Inception-v1 in our exposition. Later the Inception architecture was reﬁned in various ways, ﬁrst by the introduction of batch normaliza- tion [6] (Inception-v2) by Ioffe et al. Later the architecture was improved by additional factorization ideas in the third iteration [15] which will be referred to as Inception-v3 in this report. Conv + Relu activation Relu activation Conv

Pure Inception blocks Our older Inception models used to be trained in a par- titioned manner, where each replica was partitioned into a multiple sub-networks in order to be able to ﬁt the whole model in memory. However, the Inception architecture is highly tunable, meaning that there are a lot of possible changes to the number of ﬁlters in the various layers that do not affect the quality of the fully trained network. In order to optimize the training speed, we used to tune the layer sizes carefully in order to balance the computation be- tween the various model sub-networks. In contrast, with the introduction of TensorFlow our most recent models can be trained without partitioning the replicas. This is enabled in part by recent optimizations of memory used by backprop- agation, achieved by carefully considering what tensors are needed for gradient computation and structuring the compu-

tation to reduce the number of such tensors. Historically, we have been relatively conservative about changing the archi- tectural choices and restricted our experiments to varying isolated network components while keeping the rest of the network stable. Not simplifying earlier choices resulted in networks that looked more complicated that they needed to be. In our newer experiments, for Inception-v4 we decided to shed this unnecessary baggage and made uniform choices for the Inception blocks for each grid size. Plase refer to

All the convolutions not marked with “V” in the ﬁgures are same-padded meaning that their output grid matches the size of their input. Convolutions marked with “V” are valid padded, meaning that input patch of each unit is fully contained in the previous layer and the grid size of the output activation map is reduced accord- ingly. 3.2. Residual Inception Blocks For the residual versions of the Inception networks, we use cheaper Inception blocks than the original Inception. Each Inception block is followed by ﬁlter-expansion layer (1 × 1 convolution without activation) which is used for scaling up the dimensionality of the ﬁlter bank before the addition to match the depth of the input. This is needed to compensate for the dimensionality reduction induced by the Inception block. We tried several versions of the residual version of In- ception. Only two of them are detailed here. This could not be prevented, neither by lowering the learn- ing rate, nor by adding an extra batch-normalization to this layer. Conclusions We have presented three new network architectures in detail: • Inception-ResNet-v1: a hybrid Inception version that has a similar computational cost to Inception-v3 from [15]. • Inception-ResNet-v2: a costlier hybrid Inception ver- sion with signiﬁcantly improved recognition perfor- mance. • Inception-v4: a pure Inception variant without residual connections with roughly the same recognition perfor- mance as Inception-ResNet-v2. We studied how the introduction of residual connections leads to dramatically improved training speed for the Incep- tion architecture. Also our latest models (with and without residual connections) outperform all our previous networks, just by virtue of the increased model size.
